title: Impact of Tourism
summary: Tourism moves people, so it needs transport, accommodation, food and guides, and it brings tourists into contact with the local land and people. The impacts are grouped as economic, socio-cultural, political and environmental, and each has a positive and a negative side. India's variety of landscape, climate, monuments, religious places and adventure sites favours tourism: south India is sought in winter and the Himalayas in summer.

Positive: income and growth of allied sectors; foreign exchange (helps the balance of trade); government revenue from taxes, entry fees, tolls and import duty; jobs for guides, hotel staff, taxi drivers and craftspeople; investment in infrastructure; livelihood in the informal sector (street vendors, rickshaw pullers, tea stalls) that pumps money into the local economy.

Negative: hidden costs and leakage of profit to richer countries (goods are imported, and in all-inclusive packages about two-thirds of the spending goes to airlines, hotels and international companies); price rises that hurt local people; higher land and service costs; seasonal, insecure jobs; displacement of people for airports, resorts and reserves.

Culture covers manners, morals, beliefs, behaviour, values and norms. Positive: meeting people of other cultures, education and cultural exchange, less prejudice and tension, better community facilities, pride in heritage, demand for local arts and crafts as souvenirs, and festivals kept alive.

Negative: weaker family bonds and more nuclear families, urbanisation and emigration, friction over overcrowding, drug abuse and prostitution, exploitation of children and young women, commercialisation of traditional welcome, loss of cultural identity, crime from greed, youth imitating tourists (smoking, drinking, gambling), tourists breaking local norms, erosion of local language, cultural clashes and a widening gap between haves and have-nots.

Politics affects tourism more than tourism affects politics. A tourism policy is a set of rules, guidelines and directives for developing and promoting tourism. Positive: political stability, law and order, protection of tourists, political will to build infrastructure, tourist-targeted planning, beautification without altering the landscape. Negative: political instability and conflict, travel advisories and warnings from tourists' home governments, terrorism, naxal activity and communal conflict (the unrest in the Kashmir valley reduced tourism), and an unfavourable policy. Risk perception influences where tourists choose to go.

Negative: change in land use, loss of forest and farmland, soil erosion, landslides and floods on mountain slopes, loss of biodiversity, depletion and pollution of water, air and land, pollution of beaches, lakes and rivers, congestion, solid waste and sewage, emissions from flights and local transport, damage to heritage sites, pressure on fragile mountain areas, litter on trekking paths, disturbance of animals in parks and sanctuaries, trampling of vegetation and visual clutter from tall buildings.

Positive: environmental awareness, funds for conservation and beautification, cleanliness drives, protective measures, ecological balance as an objective, research on the effects of tourism, awareness among local people, protection of monuments and museums, parks and gardens, and the renovation of buildings and reuse of degraded land.

Sustainable tourism keeps resources and local features available for all time and does not degrade the environment. It balances economic, socio-cultural and environmental factors (three tridents; four pillars if society is split into social and cultural). Tourist carrying capacity (UNWTO) is the maximum number of people who can visit a destination at the same time without harming its physical, economic and socio-cultural environment or the quality of life.

India's tourism policy follows the 7-S mantras: Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information), Suvidha (facilitation), Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation), Sanrachnaa (infrastructure) and Safai (cleanliness).

objective: Fill in the blanks. (a) The four main impacts of tourism are economic, socio-cultural, political and ________. (b) The 7-S mantra 'Safai' means ________.
Identify whether True or False. (a) Political impacts are seen more on tourism than tourism impacts on politics. (b) All-inclusive package tours always benefit the local economy most.
(a) True. (b) False: most of the money goes to airlines, hotels and international companies.
Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the foundation of attitude. (b) Societal sustainability can be divided into social and ________.
Identify True or False. (a) Tourism helps keep local arts and crafts alive through the sale of souvenirs. (b) Terrorism increases the chance of developing tourism.
(a) True. (b) False: it reduces the chance.
Answer in one word. (a) Which organisation defined tourist carrying capacity? (b) Name one country region where general unrest reduced tourism significantly.
(a) UNWTO (United Nations World Tourism Organisation). (b) The Kashmir valley (India).

vsa: Write any two positive economic impacts of tourism.
Tourism earns foreign exchange for the country and creates jobs for guides, hoteliers, taxi drivers and craftspeople. It also brings tax revenue to the government.
State any two negative economic impacts of tourism.
Tourism raises prices and land values at the destination, which hurts local people. Much of the profit leaks to richer countries through imports and foreign-owned hotels.
Explain any two positive socio-cultural impacts of tourism.
Cultural exchange between hosts and guests reduces prejudice and brings understanding. Demand for souvenirs and interest in festivals help keep local arts, crafts and traditions alive.
Explain any two negative socio-cultural impacts of tourism.
Local youth imitate tourists by smoking, drinking and gambling, and the local culture and identity are lost. Overcrowding and tourists breaking local customs cause friction between hosts and guests.
Why do governments of tourist-sending countries issue travel advisories?
Where there is political instability, conflict or terrorism, law and order is weak and tourists are unsafe. The advisory warns their citizens not to go, or to leave at once.
What is meant by sustainable tourism?
It is tourism developed and kept in an area so that its resources and features continue for all times to come. It does not degrade or alter the environment.
It is the maximum number of people who can visit a destination at the same time without damaging its physical, economic and socio-cultural environment or reducing the quality of life (UNWTO).
Mention any two negative environmental impacts of tourism.
Pollution of water, air and land and the generation of solid waste, and the loss of forest cover and biodiversity because of construction and heavy footfall.
Name the 7-S mantras of India's tourism policy.
Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information), Suvidha (facilitation), Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation), Sanrachnaa (infrastructure) and Safai (cleanliness).
sa: Mention any three negative environmental impacts of tourism at destination places.

(i) Land use changes, forests are cleared and farmland is replaced by hotels and roads, causing soil erosion and landslides. (ii) Pollution of beaches, lakes, rivers and air, and heavy solid waste and sewage. (iii) Disturbance of wildlife and trampling of vegetation on trekking trails, leading to loss of biodiversity.

or: Mention any three positive socio-cultural impacts of tourism at destination places.

(i) Cultural exchange between tourists and hosts increases understanding and reduces prejudice. (ii) Community facilities and services improve and are used by local people. (iii) Souvenir sales and festivals keep arts, crafts and traditions alive and give pride in heritage.

sa: Explain any three positive economic impacts of tourism.

(i) It earns foreign exchange and helps the balance of trade. (ii) The government earns revenue through taxes, entry fees and import duty. (iii) It creates jobs, including informal ones, and encourages investment in infrastructure.
Explain how political stability and instability affect tourism (three points).

(i) Stability and safety attract tourists, and good law and order helps their inflow. (ii) Instability, terrorism or conflict makes tourists avoid the place and their governments issue advisories. (iii) Government policy and political will to build infrastructure decide how tourism grows.
Explain any three negative socio-cultural impacts of tourism.

(i) Loss of cultural identity, local language and traditions through imitation of tourists. (ii) Drug abuse, crime and exploitation of children and women increase at some places. (iii) Tourists breaking local norms and the gap between haves and have-nots cause conflict and tension.
Describe three ways in which tourism can improve the environment.

(i) Income from tourists funds conservation, cleanliness drives and beautification. (ii) Monuments, parks and gardens are protected and degraded land is put to use. (iii) Local people and tourists become aware of the need to protect the environment and sustainable practices are promoted.
la: Describe the positive and negative impacts of tourism, giving at least three points for each, in six points.

Positive: (i) Foreign exchange and government revenue. (ii) Jobs, including in the informal sector. (iii) Cultural exchange that reduces prejudice and keeps arts and festivals alive. Negative: (i) Higher prices and leakage of profit to richer countries. (ii) Pollution, waste and damage to forests and wildlife. (iii) Loss of cultural identity, crime and conflict between hosts and tourists.
'The environment is under great strain due to increasing tourism.' Explain the statement in six points.

(i) Forests and farmland are cleared for hotels, roads and garbage disposal. (ii) Roads on slopes cause soil erosion, landslides and floods. (iii) Water, air and land are polluted and resources are depleted. (iv) Flights and local transport release carbon dioxide and other gases. (v) Heavy footfall damages heritage sites, trampling vegetation and disturbing wildlife in sanctuaries. (vi) Waste, sewage and litter are hard to manage and congestion exceeds the carrying capacity.
Explain sustainable tourism and the 7-S mantras of India's tourism policy in six points.

(i) Sustainable tourism keeps resources available for all time without degrading the environment. (ii) It balances economic, socio-cultural and environmental factors. (iii) The area's carrying capacity must not be crossed. (iv) The 7-S mantras are Swagat (welcome), Soochanaa (information) and Suvidha (facilitation). (v) Suraksha (security), Sahyog (cooperation) and Sanrachnaa (infrastructure). (vi) Safai (cleanliness) completes the policy, and balance among all these factors sustains tourism.
